newsitem.title: GERMANY: MGAM-Horlick meeting with Deutsche just "courtesy".
newsitem.headline: MGAM-Horlick meeting with Deutsche just "courtesy".

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Friday that it had only acted out of courtesy in arranging a meeting for Nicola Horlick with legal representatives from its parent Deutsche Bank AG.
DMG spokesman Markus Will said in response to a Reuter enquiry that matters relating to her former employment should be addressed through Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).

"Nicola Horlick requested a meeting at Deutsche Bank in Frankfurt and as a matter of courtesy we arranged for her to meet with representatives from the legal and personnel departments of Deutsche," Will said.
"Until her resignation yesterday Mrs Horlick worked for MGAM and we have explained that matters relating to her former employment should be addressed to MGAM."
Horlick, former head of British pension fund business at MGAM, responded by telling Reuters that she was very upset at MGAM's statement and wanted clarification immediately.
Horlick had earlier said she had had a "fair hearing" in two-hour meeting with members of Deutsche Bank's legal and personnel departments in Frankfurt.
Asked by a Reuter reporter at Frankfurt airport how she reacted to MGAM's latest statement, Horlick said:
"If Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is now saying these talks were irrelevant then naturally I am very upset and want clarification.
"The impression I got (from the talks in Frankfurt) was that the people we spoke to were to mediate and to examine the facts on the other side," she said.

Horlick was suspended earlier from Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asset Management this week pending the outcome of an investigation into what DMG described as "a potential breach of her contract" and Horlick resigned on Thursday.
She had flown to Frankfurt to meet Deutsche executives, saying she wanted her job back and charging that her suspension had been based on "hearsay." (( -- Frankfurt Newsroom + 49 69 756525 ))
